Do Low Rolling Resistance Tires Actually Save Gas? Data, RRC & Payback Analysis

By EcoDriver Editorial Board • Published Recently • 5 min read
⚡ Direct Answer

Low Rolling Resistance (LRR) tires reduce passenger vehicle fuel consumption by 3% to 5% (and EV energy consumption by 4% to 8%) by lowering the tire Rolling Resistance Coefficient (RRC) from conventional baseline levels of 0.0105 down to 0.0065–0.0075 through advanced silica tread compounds and stiffer sidewalls.

undefined

Frequently Asked Questions

Do low rolling resistance tires have worse grip in the rain?

Modern second- and third-generation LRR tires match conventional tires in wet braking performance because synthetic silica formulations maintain chemical adhesion on wet asphalt without increasing viscoelastic hysteresis on dry surfaces.

Do LRR tires wear out faster than standard tires?

Tread wear depends on the specific Uniform Tire Quality Grading (UTQG) treadwear rating. High-grade LRR touring tires from Tier-1 manufacturers (e.g. Michelin, Continental, Bridgestone) feature treadwear ratings of 600 to 700 with warranties extending between 60,000 and 70,000 miles.

Does tire pressure affect rolling resistance more than the tire compound?

Yes. Running a tire underinflated by just 5 PSI increases rolling resistance by 10%, entirely negating the fuel efficiency advantages of an LRR compound. Maintaining manufacturer door-jamb cold inflation pressure is critical.
